clue.text: Part of payslip I query showing resentment

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An employee squints at a payslip and fires off an irritated question about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pique is a fit of wounded pride, so a person in that state is displaying resentment.

clue.text: Drama, three-quarters complete, that's light-hearted

parts.note: a drama is a play

indicators.note: keep three of the four letters of the synonym for complete, dropping its final one

parts.note: complete means full

explanation.surface: A theatre piece that is three-quarters finished turns out to be a comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: something playful is jokey and frivolous in spirit.

clue.text: Unusual or quite insane survey

indicators.note: unusual suggests the letters of the following words appear in an odd new order

explanation.surface: A survey's questions strike someone as strange or downright mad.
explanation.definitionFit: A survey is conducted by handing out a printed list of questions to respondents.

clue.text: Single judge supports divorcee — that's clear

indicators.note: in a down clue the single judge sits underneath, holding up the former spouse

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse
single means one
to judge is to rate

explanation.surface: A lone judge backs a divorced person, and the matter seems settled.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'supports' puts ONE RATE below EX.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear someone of blame or guilt is to absolve them, a synonym.

clue.text: Another helping for a short time

definitions.meaning: a second plateful of food at a meal
a brief moment, as in 'back in a few ticks'

explanation.surface: A diner asks for more food, but only briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are standard senses: a further portion of food, and brief moments of time.

clue.text: Force to leave spot on holiday

parts.note: to spot is to see
someone off work is away on holiday

explanation.surface: Someone is told to go after being noticed while away on vacation.
explanation.definitionFit: To see off an intruder or rival is to chase them away, an idiom.

clue.text: Bob's share

definitions.meaning: a bob is a short hairstyle, a kind of haircut
a portion of the takings, as in 'your slice'

explanation.surface: It is about the portion of money owed to a man called Bob.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is a style of haircut, and one's share of loot is one's cut.

clue.text: In essence book where we see protected flora and fauna

definitions.text: where we see protected flora and fauna

parts.note: the essence of something is its nature
to book is to reserve

explanation.surface: A book at heart about protected plants and wildlife.
explanation.definitionFit: A nature reserve is a designated area where wildlife and habitats are safeguarded.

clue.text: Bias found in South London gardens

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
Kew Gardens are the Royal Botanic Gardens in south-west London

explanation.surface: Prejudice is uncovered in the gardens of south London.
explanation.walkthrough: KEW is the Royal Botanic Gardens in London.
explanation.definitionFit: To skew something is to slant or distort it, a bias.

clue.text: After a new warning sent back English plant

indicators.note: the reversed portion follows the letter given by a
the word for new plus the word for warning are read backwards

parts.note: an omen is a warning sign

explanation.surface: Following a fresh alert, an English plant is returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns N plus OMEN into NEMON, which follows A and precedes E.
explanation.definitionFit: The anemone, or windflower, is a flowering plant of the buttercup family.

clue.text: Type of square covered by piece in Scrabble championship

indicators.note: the letter for the square sits inside, enclosed by the game piece

parts.note: Scrabble letters are on small tiles
a T-square is a draughtsman's ruler

explanation.surface: A Scrabble tournament where one special square is hidden beneath a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: A T-square is a T-shaped ruler used in technical drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporting title is the championship held by the winner.

clue.text: Respected older man with plump lady's physique

parts.note: plump means fat
a lady's belongings are hers, the possessive her
a person's physique is their figure

explanation.surface: A distinguished gentleman paired with a rather heavy-set woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A father figure is an older man looked up to as a mentor or guide.

clue.text: Fresh opportunity for the rest of the actors

parts.note: fresh means green, as in new or inexperienced
room means scope or opportunity, as in 'room for improvement'

explanation.surface: A new chance is offered to the remaining members of the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the rest of the actors' seems to mean the remaining cast; read it as the place actors rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A green room is the theatre lounge where performers relax off stage.

clue.text: Husband and a kid about to get cleaner in bath

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so these letters run in reverse

parts.note: to kid someone is to fool them

explanation.surface: A husband and child are about to be scrubbed clean in the tub.
explanation.definitionFit: A loofah is a dried fibrous gourd used as a scrubbing sponge.

clue.text: Name of Conservative journalist rolling in it (not Henry)

parts.note: ED is short for editor, a journalist

indicators.note: not says the letter for Henry is left out of the word for wealthy

parts.note: someone rolling in it is rich
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A wealthy Tory journalist is named, with Henry excluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' drops H from RICH, leaving RIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Cedric is a male first name, so it is an example of a name.

clue.text: Extremely crude about new dance beat

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the outer pair goes round the rest
extremely points to the outermost letters, the first and last of crude
new tells us the word dance is rearranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A rather vulgar new dance routine is set to a beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' here means surrounding, not circa (CA): the outer letters of crude wrap the rearranged dance, signalled by 'new'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadence is rhythm, the regular beat or measured flow of sound.

clue.text: Relative with money going round America

indicators.note: the coin encircles the abbreviation for America

parts.note: a coin is money
US is short for United States, America

explanation.surface: A family member travels around the States with cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin is a family member, the child of an aunt or uncle.

clue.text: Rude sign once possibly not regarded as official?

indicators.note: possibly hints at one possible rearrangement of the letters in the preceding words

explanation.surface: An obscene gesture, once perhaps, that lacked official sanction.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not formally acknowledged by authorities lacks recognition, so it is unacknowledged.

clue.text: Jack indisposed to find girl

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in playing cards
indisposed means ill

explanation.surface: Jack is poorly and goes in search of a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme pairing of Jack and Jill gives the surface its charm.
explanation.definitionFit: Jill is a girl's name, and in old use a jill is a girl or sweetheart.

clue.text: Holiday island — one with business area

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
biz is slang for business, as in showbiz

explanation.surface: A holiday resort described as an island with a commercial district.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is a Balearic island in the Mediterranean, famous as a holiday destination.

clue.text: Ambassador concealing fuss

indicators.note: concealing says the answer is tucked away inside the word ambassador

explanation.definitionFit: Ado means bustle or commotion, as in 'much ado about nothing'.

clue.text: Large pouch parson damaged crossing centre of Perth

indicators.note: the jumbled clergyman goes over and around the letter from Perth
damaged signals the letters of parson are knocked into a different order
centre of picks the middle letter of the Scottish city's name

explanation.surface: A clergyman's big bag is wrecked as he travels through central Perth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' gives SPORAN from PARSON; 'crossing' puts it around R. A sporran is the pouch worn on the front of a Scottish kilt, apt with Perth in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporran is a large leather or fur pouch worn at the front of a kilt.

clue.text: After pork-pie decided initially to have short rest

indicators.note: the remaining letters come after the fib

parts.note: pork pie is Cockney rhyming slang for lie

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of decided

parts.note: to have something is to own it

explanation.surface: After eating a pork pie, someone decides on a brief nap.
explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang, 'pork pie' means a lie (often shortened to 'porky').
explanation.definitionFit: A lie-down is a brief nap or recline, a short break for resting.

clue.text: Expression of disagreement with setter's view

parts.note: the setter refers to themself, so the setter's means my
an eye is a viewpoint or opinion, as in 'in my eye'

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler voices dissent, giving their own opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: 'My eye!' is an old-fashioned exclamation of disbelief, an idiom meaning nonsense.
